claims.statement: The root cause is not a defect in allocation rule v18 itself, but the carrier system's inability to process pickup confirmations at the rate/volume that v18 generates, causing a 47-minute confirmation lag that exceeds the 30-minute slot window.
claims.corroboration: Handoff trace (m8_r_handoffs) shows v18 orders (EXC-0921) have 47-minute confirmation lag while non-v18 orders have normal lag. The lag is specific to v18 orders and the booking rate/pattern they create, not a carrier system outage. One re-booked order (after carrier refresh) received valid slot, confirming the system is functional but overwhelmed.
claims.limitation: Root cause is the interaction between v18 volume and carrier capacity, not a failure in either system alone. Mitigation can address this by either: (1) adjusting slot windows to accommodate the lag (requires specific feed identification), or (2) changing the volume pattern by reverting v18.

capability_gaps.reason: Confirm_with_carrier_ops returned procedural requirements but not the specific feed ID needed for apply_slot_correction. Without this, a second slot correction attempt risks the same misapplication as R2.

next_action.rationale: Allocation rule v18 (east-node-first reservation priority) creates a booking volume/pattern that overwhelms the carrier confirmation system's 47-minute lag tolerance. Reverting to the prior rule set will restore the booking pattern that had no lag (as shown by non-EXC-0921 orders before 05:58), eliminating the trigger for the carrier lag. This is reversible and idempotent, scoped to east-node reservation priority as specified in the gate conditions. After reversion, replay_held_allocations can re-allocate the 186 orders under the old rule without slot conflicts.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Reverting v18 will change the allocation booking pattern and volume on east-node routes, relieving pressure on the carrier confirmation system and allowing the 186 held orders to be re-allocated and successfully picked up.
